page: Amazon Web Services m8id.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, backed by a large 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This variant includes 474 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks show strong results in single-threaded execution and specialized instruction sets. The Intel processor supports AMX tile and int8 instructions, AVX-512 variants, and hardware-level cryptography. Geekbench text processing reaches the top tier bracket at 2,981 points, complemented by strong single-core scores of 2,207. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also place in the top quartile at 34.23 GB/sec and 14.58 GB/sec respectively. General multi-core throughput, static web serving at 15.52 GB/sec, and Redis operations at 15.29 million ops/sec remain aligned with average expected output for an 8-vCPU footprint.

The inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage provides low-latency ephemeral I/O compared to purely network-attached volume configurations, improving resource density for storage-bound tasks without requiring specialized storage instances. The primary tradeoff lies in the ephemeral nature of the local drive and moderate baseline networking throughput. The server is well positioned for relational databases with local caching requirements, CI/CD artifact building, web application backends, and moderate data manipulation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.2xlarge is a general-purpose x86_64 cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running on the Nitro hypervisor. It offers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 3.9 GHz, 32 GB of DDR5 memory, and 474 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage with 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX int8, and hardware crypto acceleration. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, notably in Geekbench single-core, text processing, and compression routines, alongside steady multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. By packaging local NVMe storage within a balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM configuration, this instance delivers effective hardware density for caching layers, database engines, continuous integration workers, and containerized backend microservices that demand fast ephemeral storage without over-provisioning compute capacity.
